questions.question: What does adding "use client" at the top of a module do?
options: Makes the component skip server-side rendering entirely
Marks the module as an entry point into the client bundle, so it and everything it imports ship to the browser
Turns the module's functions into Server Functions
Only enables useState in that single component
questions.explanation: "use client" defines a boundary. The module and its imports become client code. Client Components are still server-rendered to HTML, then hydrated.

questions.question: Which prop CANNOT be passed from a Server Component to a Client Component?
options: A plain object of strings and numbers
An ordinary arrow function used as an event handler
questions.explanation: Props crossing the boundary are serialised. Ordinary functions cannot be serialised; Server Functions are the exception because React passes a reference.

questions.question: How can a Client Component display a Server Component?
options: By receiving it already rendered as a prop such as children
It is impossible in any form
questions.explanation: Client Components cannot import Server Components, but a server parent can pass server-rendered JSX to them via children or other props.

questions.question: Why must every Server Function check authentication and validate its arguments?
options: Server Functions run in the browser
They are effectively public endpoints that anyone can call with arbitrary arguments
React refuses to call unvalidated functions
questions.explanation: Calling a Server Function is a network request. Hiding a button doesn't stop a direct call, and types are erased at runtime.
